content.text:
I have both documents in the prompt — no file reads needed. Here's my check.

**Summary:** The brief is clean. All ten key facts are stated correctly on the right basis and period, and every atomic claim I extracted is supported by the release. Two notes for the analyst rather than errors:

- **f07** is only partially covered: the ~$10 billion of 2026 repurchases appears in the lead, but the brief never places it inside the ~$24 billion of planned repurchases over 2026-2028 (it cites only the broader $45 billion+ total capital return). The figure it does give is correct.
- **f10**: the net-add figures are exact, but the brief drops the release's characterization of 646,000 as a *record* quarter for combined fiber and fixed wireless — a lost positive, not a misstatement.
- Rounding checks that pass: Legacy revenue $1,632M → "$1.6 billion"; Advanced Connectivity service revenue $23,478M → "$23.5 billion"; operating income $7,345M → "$7.3 billion".
- Basis labels are handled correctly throughout: adjusted EPS, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted operating income, free cash flow, capital investment and net debt are each tagged non-GAAP, and GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations is kept distinct from the $0.65 adjusted figure.
- The three "Watch items" are recommendations, but each carries an embedded factual assertion (held-for-sale subsidiary, spectrum-related abandonment charge, 2.5x net-debt target post-EchoStar), and all three trace to the release, including footnote 1.

facts.evidence: Revenues totaled $31.6 billion, up 2.3% from the year-ago quarter, driven by growth in Advanced Connectivity fiber and wireless revenues.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66, compared to $0.62 in the year-ago quarter
adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) was $0.65, versus $0.54 in the prior year period
Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion
adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $12.3 billion, up 5.2% year over year
reiterating full-year guidance ... Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) is guided to $2.25 to $2.35 in 2026, with a double-digit 3-year CAGR through 2028.
reiterating full-year guidance while accelerating share repurchases to approximately $10 billion
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $4.7 billion, compared to $4.4 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% year over year to $1.6 billion as the company continues to decommission its copper-based network.

The segment added 646,000 total consumer and business internet net adds, comprising 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless connections. Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000, with postpaid phone churn of 0.86%.

claims.claim: AT&T reported Q2 2026 revenue of $31.6 billion.
AT&T reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.65.
AT&T reiterated its full-year guidance.
AT&T is accelerating share repurchases to approximately $10 billion.
Revenues totaled $31.6 billion, up 2.3% from the year-ago quarter.
The revenue increase was driven by growth in Advanced Connectivity fiber and wireless revenues.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66, compared to $0.62 in the year-ago quarter.
Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) was $0.65, versus $0.54 in the prior year period.
Operating income was $7.0 billion.
Adjusted operating income (non-GAAP) was $7.5 billion.
Income from continuing operations was $5.0 billion, up 3.6% year over year.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $12.3 billion, up 5.2% year over year.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $4.7 billion, compared to $4.4 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew 5.1% year over year to $23.5 billion.
Advanced Connectivity operating income was up 20.3% year over year to $7.3 billion.
The Advanced Connectivity segment added 646,000 total consumer and business internet net adds, comprising 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless connections.
Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000, with postpaid phone churn of 0.86%.
Legacy segment revenues declined 25.9% year over year to $1.6 billion.
The Legacy revenue decline reflects the company's continued decommissioning of its copper-based network.
AT&T reiterates its long-term outlook for 2026-2028.
The outlook includes adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) growth of 3% to 4% in 2026, improving to 5% or better in 2028.
Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) is guided to $2.25 to $2.35 in 2026, with a double-digit 3-year CAGR through 2028.
The company expects to return $45 billion or more to shareholders during 2026-2028 through dividends and share repurchases.
Total debt was $144.0 billion at the end of the second quarter.
Net debt (non-GAAP) was $126.4 billion.
Capital expenditures related to continuing operations were $5.7 billion.
Capital investment (non-GAAP) was $6.1 billion.
The company returned $4.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter, including approximately $2.2 billion in common share repurchases.
AT&T plans to sell a controlling interest in the subsidiary holding the acquired Lumen mass markets fiber business, and that subsidiary is currently classified as held-for-sale.
There was an asset abandonment charge associated with the reprioritization of the company's spectrum strategy.

AT&T expects its net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio (non-GAAP) to return to a level consistent with its target in the 2.5x range within approximately three years following the closing of the EchoStar transaction.
